concepts.title: Internal Assessment Mark Structure
concepts.definition: The internal assessment carries 20 marks split evenly between project work and practical work, and each of those halves again splits into a record-plus-performance component and a year-end presentation-or-test component, five marks at each of the four corners.
concepts.key_idea: Four boxes of five marks: project record, project viva, practical performance, practical test.

solution_steps.explain: project record plus the year end presentation and viva

concepts.title: Spreadsheet Average of a Data Range
concepts.definition: The spreadsheet AVERAGE cell formula computes the mean of a highlighted data range: it adds every cell in the range and divides by the number of entries, exactly the hand arithmetic of an average.
concepts.key_idea: AVERAGE is just sum of the range divided by how many cells it holds.

solution_steps.action: add up every entry in the range
solution_steps.explain: the spreadsheet does this inside the AVERAGE formula; here the total is the sum of the column

solution_steps.action: divide by the number of entries
solution_steps.explain: the mean shown in the result cell

concepts.title: Spreadsheet Practical: Simple Interest Cell
concepts.definition: The listed spreadsheet practical computes simple interest at given rates for given periods: principal, rate and years sit in labelled cells and the interest cell multiplies them with the percent conversion.
concepts.key_idea: One cell formula reproduces the whole simple interest table row.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_013_practical_project.txt, suggested practicals: compute simple and compound interest at given rates for given periods
question_patterns: in the interest practical the sheet holds 4000 at 5 percent for 3 years; compute the simple interest cell

solution_steps.action: multiply principal, rate and period with the percent conversion
solution_steps.explain: the fixed fraction of the principal per year times the years

concepts.title: Compound Interest Growth Across Rows
concepts.definition: The compound interest practical fills one spreadsheet row per period: each row multiplies the previous balance by one plus the rate, so the balance column grows geometrically and the final cell holds the accumulated amount.
concepts.key_idea: Each row applies the same multiplier to the row above; the factor is one plus the rate raised to the row count.

concepts.title: Pictograph Symbol Counts
concepts.definition: A pictograph shows data by repeating a picture symbol, each standing for a fixed number of items. The number of symbols needed for an amount is the amount divided by the value of one symbol.
concepts.key_idea: Divide the quantity by what one picture stands for; draw that many symbols.

solution_steps.action: divide the quantity by the value of one symbol
solution_steps.explain: the count of picture symbols the row must display

concepts.title: Pie Chart Sector Angles
concepts.definition: A pie chart spends the full 360 degrees of a circle among the categories, giving each a sector angle equal to its share of the total times 360.
concepts.key_idea: Share of the whole times 360 degrees is the slice to draw.

concepts.title: Choosing Between Pie and Bar Charts
concepts.definition: Each chart answers a different question: a pie chart shows how one whole splits into shares, a bar graph lines categories up for comparison by height, and a pictograph keeps counts concrete with repeated symbols. Picking the chart is matching the question to the display.
concepts.key_idea: Shares of one whole go to the pie; category against category goes to the bars.
